Moved up from 26: reaches HTTP framing states that were previously unreachable for the fuzzer, i.e. coverage of untrusted-input paths.

Moved up 5: it corrects a benchmark that silently measured nothing, which is a misleading-signal fix.
Moved up 6: unblocks running local CI containers in parallel, a concrete recurring developer blocker.

Raised 8 places: it is at least a genuine helper defect, unlike the purely stylistic cleanups below it.

inconsistencies: #35713 (full Boost.Test removal), #35139 (in-tree ASSERT macros) and #36091 (debug printers for tested types) all reshape unit-test assertions and diagnostics; #36091 says its printers are intended for #35713. Review #35713 first to settle the runner direction, then #35139 and #36091 as follow-ups, otherwise the three will duplicate each other's macro/printer layers.

#32554 removes the embedded block413567.raw benchmark fixture while #36254 adds undo data for that same fixture; the bench fixture strategy has to be decided before either lands, and #32554 also supersedes #32457.
#35442 bundles and depends on #35433 (deprecating the replaceable RPC arguments); it cannot merge ahead of that PR.
#36074 (add util/check.h includes) and #36087 (AssertUnreachable + linters) both do repo-wide scripted assertion edits and will conflict with each other and with #35713/#35139; sequence them.

#36098 (corpus reachability goals) and #36129 (chainman reset in load_external_block_file) both target corpus-replay trustworthiness and are complementary: #36129 makes replay order-independent, which is a precondition for reachability goals to be meaningful.
#35774 and #36024 are the same underlying problem from two sides - release-like platform binaries whose test results are untested or invisible; review them together.
#35356 is blocked by a wallet_signer path-handling bug that belongs to the wallet area; the framework-side change cannot go green alone.
#32409 is NACKed as dead code and #35994's author prefers abandoning it; both are closure candidates rather than review targets.
result.notes: No P1 assigned: none of these 45 describes a problem whose persistence for another release cycle would be seriously harmful (no active flaky-test breakage, no blocked category-defining project waiting on a decision). The P2 group is the test-infrastructure work with durable reach (runner replacement, consensus-level unit coverage, untested release binaries, fuzz-corpus coverage regressions); the large P3 band is ordered signal fixes first, then high-risk-path coverage and measured speedups, then bench/ergonomics; P4 is style, docs and dead or abandoned changes.
